question: The effect of a drug that acts as a competitive inhibitor in an enzymatic reaction:

options.opa: It can be canceled with substrate concentrations much higher than the concentration of the inhibitor.
options.opb: It does not affect the kinetic constants of the reaction.
options.opc: The higher the concentration of the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex present, the greater.
options.opd: It consists of a reduction in the apparent metabolization constant and an increase in the rate of catalysis.

analysis: A competitive inhibitor competes with the substrate for binding to the active site of the enzyme. This type of inhibition can be overcome by increasing the concentration of the substrate, as it can outcompete the inhibitor for binding to the enzyme.
